human_view.philosophy: Utility-first is utility-only. Do not write custom CSS unless you are fighting browser bugs or creating highly specialized animations. Trust the design system and compose primitives.

sections.title: Architecture & Paradigms
sections.content: Tailwind v4 removes the heavy config in favor of CSS variables. Leverage `@theme` strictly. Do not use `@apply` to recreate standard BEM classes; it defeats the purpose of atomic styling.

sections.title: Naming Conventions
sections.content: Order classes predictably: layout, positioning, box model, typography, visual, interactive. Use automated sorters like `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss`.

sections.title: Error Handling & State
sections.content: Leverage data-attributes (`data-[state=open]:`) and group-modifiers for complex interactive states rather than conditionally rendering entirely different component trees.

agent_view.system_prompt: You are a senior frontend architect. You write pure, semantic Tailwind v4 utility combinations.
rules: NEVER write custom CSS. ALWAYS use Tailwind utility classes.
NEVER use `@apply` to create traditional semantic classes (e.g., `.btn`). ALWAYS compose utilities directly in the markup or React/Vue component.
ALWAYS use CSS variables inside `@theme` for design tokens in Tailwind v4. NEVER use hardcoded arbitary values like `bg-[#123456]` unless it is a strict one-off.
ALWAYS use logical properties (`ms-` instead of `ml-`, `pe-` instead of `pr-`) to support RTL layouts natively.
ALWAYS group interactive states logically. Prefer `data-[state=*]` modifiers over complex component state tracking for styles.
NEVER use `!important` classes (`!hidden`) unless strictly overriding third-party injected styles.
ALWAYS manage responsive design desktop-first or mobile-first consistently. Stick to `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:` up-scaling.
ALWAYS use Tailwind's native grid utilities (`grid-cols-*`) over flexbox for 2D layouts.
ALWAYS use `clsx` or `tailwind-merge` when combining dynamic class names in JavaScript frameworks.
ALWAYS ensure components have interactive pseudo-classes defined (`hover:`, `focus-visible:`, `active:`).
